records.scientific_question: For an unweighted planar graph G and pairwise disjoint terminal sets S1={s}, S2={t}, S3={a,b}, can the minimum number of edges whose deletion separates every pair of distinct terminal sets while keeping the two terminals in S3 connected be computed in polynomial time?
records.source_baseline: Bentert et al. (ICALP 2024), Theorem 1: planar Two-Sets Cut-Uncut is solvable by a one-sided-error randomized algorithm in 2^(|S|+|T|) n^O(1) time, but the paper explicitly leaves the three-set planar case with two singleton sets and one two-vertex set open. Fixed-k planar Multiway Cut is polynomial, but it does not impose this uncut connectivity constraint.
records.exact_event: By 2030-12-31, a publicly accessible primary theorem gives an exact polynomial-time algorithm for the specified planar unweighted Three-Sets Cut-Uncut problem, with runtime polynomial in |V(G)|+|E(G)| and success probability at least 2/3 on every input if randomized. The algorithm must either return the optimum cut size and a realizing edge set or correctly report infeasibility. A special case, approximation, or algorithm that drops the requirement that a and b remain connected does not count.
frozen_assumptions: G is a finite simple undirected planar graph, given without requiring a fixed embedding.
S1={s}, S2={t}, and S3={a,b} are pairwise disjoint; all edge deletion costs are one.
A feasible edge set F leaves s, t, and the connected component containing a and b in three pairwise distinct connected components of G-F; a and b must remain connected.
The objective is to minimize |F|; infeasible instances must be detected.
The event concerns an exact algorithm, not a heuristic, approximation, empirical implementation, or the general nonplanar problem.
records.improvement_criterion: Resolve the explicitly stated planar (1,1,2)-terminal case with an exact polynomial-time algorithm; randomized polynomial time with a standard per-instance success probability of at least 2/3 qualifies.
records.resolution_policy: Two independent reviewers inspect the dated primary source and full proof/algorithm against every frozen assumption. A mismatched graph class, terminal pattern, weighted variant only, or relaxation is not a match. A proof of infeasibility handling and exactness is required. A search miss is not a negative; if no matching source is found by deadline, record INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE unless the separately documented source-coverage review supports an explicit unresolved-at-horizon record.
records.evidence_standard: A dated peer-reviewed article or public preprint containing a complete mathematical algorithm and correctness proof; two independent human reviewers must agree after checking the formal problem statement and proof. LLM review is not an independent reviewer.
records.ambiguity_policy: If edge/vertex deletion, weighted/unweighted costs, the S3 connectivity condition, exactness, or polynomial runtime is unclear, mark UNRESOLVED rather than count the event as achieved.

records.scientific_question: Can the constant-round k-hop dominating-set approximation bound proved for high-girth graphs of bounded k-hop expansion be achieved on all graphs of the same bounded k-hop expansion, without a girth assumption?

A restricted girth class, randomized-only theorem, or asymptotically worse ratio does not count.
frozen_assumptions: k-hop domination means every vertex is at graph distance at most k from a selected vertex; objective is minimum cardinality.

questions.problem_statement: Does general unweighted MAX BISECTION admit a polynomial-time approximation guarantee at the Goemans–Williamson MAX CUT ratio, under the same worst-case input scope?

items: Input is a finite unweighted undirected graph with even vertex count; a feasible bisection has equal-size sides.
The guarantee is worst-case over all such input graphs and is an approximation guarantee for the produced bisection, not an SDP value bound.
The approximation ratio is at least the conventional α_GW constant; no Unique Games assumption is allowed for the algorithmic upper bound.
A randomized algorithm may state the ratio in expectation, but must define that convention explicitly.

questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Austrin–Benabbas–Georgiou establish the approximately 0.8776 line of algorithms; Brakensiek et al. (SODA 2026) retain the α_GW question as open and prove that the ε-uncorrelated Basic-SDP two-stage paradigm alone cannot reach α_GW (their gap is below 0.87853). That is a limitation of this paradigm, not an impossibility for all algorithms.
questions.desired_improvement: Reach the MAX CUT α_GW approximation ratio for unrestricted unweighted MAX BISECTION, with an exact theorem and polynomial-time algorithm.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2031-12-31, a public primary theorem gives a polynomial-time algorithm for MAX BISECTION on every finite unweighted general graph whose expected cut value is at least α_GW times optimum, where α_GW is the standard Goemans–Williamson MAX CUT constant. The theorem must specify the randomized or deterministic guarantee and polynomial running time. A result only for a restricted graph class, an SDP integrality-gap statement, or a ratio strictly below α_GW does not count.

questions.required_evidence_standard: Dated primary paper or proceedings article with a complete algorithm and proof; two independent human theorem checks are required.
questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Two independent reviewers compare the full theorem, graph scope, bisection constraint, approximation ratio, runtime, and randomness convention with this frozen event. The SODA 2026 Basic-SDP obstruction alone is not success or refutation of the all-algorithms question.
questions.forecast_statement: I judge an unrestricted α_GW guarantee for MAX BISECTION by the deadline highly uncertain, with a directional lean that it will not be established by then: the latest primary result blocks an influential route, but leaves other algorithmic paradigms open.

questions.problem_statement: Can one maintain an explicit (1−ε)-approximate maximum matching under arbitrary single-edge insertions and deletions in general graphs with a fixed polynomial saving over linear amortized update time?

items: One edge insertion or deletion is one update; the graph is a general undirected n-vertex graph.
The data structure outputs the matching edges, not only an estimate of matching size.
ε and δ are positive constants independent of n; the update bound is amortized over every prefix or a clearly equivalent standard guarantee.
The adversary model and probability of maintaining a valid (1−ε)-approximation are stated in the theorem.

questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Behnezhad–Ghafari (FOCS 2024) reduce the runtime to a bound parameterized by ORS graph density and state the n^{1−Ω(1)} update-time target as a major open problem. Assadi–Khanna–Kiss (SODA 2025) further make the algorithmic bound depend directly on ORS density, but do not establish a fixed polynomial exponent unconditionally.
questions.desired_improvement: Achieve explicit near-optimal matching with a fixed n^{1−δ} amortized update-time exponent on unrestricted general graphs.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2031-12-31, a public randomized or deterministic algorithm maintains, after every update in a fully dynamic general undirected graph, an explicit matching of size at least (1−ε)·OPT for some fixed constants ε>0 and δ>0, with amortized update time O(n^{1−δ}) and polynomial preprocessing/space. The approximation must hold with high probability over every polynomial-length update sequence under a stated adversary model. A matching-size estimate alone, a bipartite-only result, or n/2^{Ω(√log n)} time without a fixed exponent δ does not count.

questions.required_evidence_standard: Primary theorem and full proof in a dated proceedings article or public preprint; independently check the data-structure output and asymptotic bound.
questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Reviewers verify that the algorithm maintains edges of a valid matching after every update, handles insertions and deletions, uses unrestricted general graphs, and has constants ε,δ independent of n. ORS-conditional bounds do not count unless they imply an unconditional fixed-exponent bound.
questions.forecast_statement: I judge an unconditional fixed-exponent update-time algorithm for explicit near-optimal dynamic matching unlikely by the deadline; recent work has sharpened the ORS reduction but still leaves the extremal density gap central.

questions.problem_statement: Does the ordered Ruzsa–Szemerédi parameter have polynomial growth for some fixed linear matching density?

items: Use the SODA 2025 definition of ORS(n,r): edge-disjoint ordered matchings of size r, each induced in the suffix union.
The constants δ and ε are fixed independently of n, and the lower bound holds for infinitely many n.
Any reversal between prefix and suffix conventions must be explicitly proved by reversing the matching order.

questions.existing_strongest_baseline: The SODA 2025 primary paper defines ORS(n,δn) using ordered edge-disjoint linear-size matchings, gives lower bounds n^{Ω(1/log log n)} and upper bounds n^{1−o(1)}, and explicitly calls closing the gap challenging. This structural parameter controls the runtime of the FOCS 2024/SODA 2025 dynamic matching algorithms.
questions.desired_improvement: Establish a polynomial lower bound ORS(n,δn)≥n^ε for some fixed positive δ,ε, or a theorem that implies it with exact constants and quantifiers.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2031-12-31, a public theorem proves that there exist constants δ>0 and ε>0 and infinitely many n for which an n-vertex graph has an ordered sequence of at least n^ε edge-disjoint matchings, each of size at least δn, where each matching is induced in the union of itself and all later matchings (equivalently, reverse the ordering convention consistently). A mere n^{o(1)} lower bound, a bound for sublinear-size matchings, or a non-ordered RS construction that does not satisfy the frozen ordered condition does not count.

questions.required_evidence_standard: Primary mathematical proof in a dated paper or proceedings version with an explicit asymptotic family or theorem.
questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Two reviewers verify the ordered induced-matching condition, linear size, graph order, constants, and infinitely-many-n quantifier from the proof. The implication to dynamic matching is reported separately and not used as the ORS label.
questions.forecast_statement: I judge a fixed polynomial lower bound for ORS(n,δn) unlikely by 2030; the known subpolynomial lower bound reflects a long-standing extremal obstruction, although an improved construction could change the dynamic-matching landscape.

items: The problem is exact worst-case Subset Sum with positive integer weights in binary and a target integer.
